decides: equality over the reals for the polynomial fragment with uninterpreted atoms: a canonical polynomial with exact rational coefficients, comparisons and conditions normalized, odd and even functions signed
limits: identities between atoms beyond parity (sin² + cos² = 1, sqrt(x)² = x) are not used, so equal terms may keep different forms; expansion is bounded
name: normal_form

rank.general: are two real functions equal wherever both are defined
rank.question: whether two terms have one canonical form: a polynomial with rational coefficients over uninterpreted atoms
rank.why: normalizing is a total computation; equality of real functions built from sin, exp and the rest is undecidable (Richardson 1968), and a difference is shown by one point, so the general question is a ∀ (Π1) for continuous functions
